source.title: Towards Understanding Generalization in Gradient-Based Meta-Learning
source.authors: Simon Guiroy; Vikas Verma; C. Pal

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent cutoff or corruption.
record.tranche_reason: Reports original results on how landscape and trajectory properties relate to generalization, but in few-shot meta-learning rather than the claim versions’ specified settings.
record.gate_note: The paper measures curvature, trajectory coherence, gradient coherence, and trajectory norm against meta-test accuracy. These results concern few-shot adaptation to new tasks; none tests a listed version’s specified setup or measure. The proposed regularizer is an induced training change and is recorded as a result about this adjacent setting.
record.test_reason: The study reports original meta-learning results, but none tests a listed version. Its closest comparison to V7 uses unscaled Hessian spectral norm and meta-test target accuracy, rather than magnitude-scaled weight perturbations and training–test generalization gaps. Using Adam, convolutional networks, and different task-batch sizes does not supply the controlled comparisons required by V3–V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report that adapted solutions become flatter, lower in support loss, and farther from the initialization during meta-training; continued flattening despite deteriorating target accuracy argues against flatness as a generalization indicator in this setting. Trajectory and gradient coherence correlate with target accuracy, motivating a regularizer that improves the tested Omniglot result.
record.recipe_differences: Few-shot gradient-based meta-learning on disjoint task classes, using MAML and First-Order MAML; it measures adaptation landscape and trajectory properties rather than the listed versions’ supervised-learning interventions or specified measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The relation between trajectory coherence and accuracy appears less linear in some settings; the finetuning baseline has different curvature and coherence trends. Results vary across dataset and task settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Adapted meta-test solutions flatten after an initial sharpening phase; in extended First-Order MAML training, they continue flattening while target accuracy deteriorates. Finetuning shows a different curvature trend.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unscaled support-loss Hessian flatness need not track few-shot meta-test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Trajectory-direction and gradient coherence correlate with meta-test target accuracy; finetuning baselines show low coherence and lower target accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Coherence across task adaptation directions or gradients is associated with generalization to new tasks in the tested meta-learning settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Trajectory-coherence regularization raises Omniglot 20-way 1-shot MAML accuracy from 94.05% to 95.38%, averaged over five trials with 600 test tasks each.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trajectory-coherence regularization can improve MAML meta-test accuracy in this setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Adaptation trajectory norm grows during MAML training, but the authors report that it does not reflect generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptation trajectory norm does not reliably indicate meta-test generalization in the tested setting.

record.problems: The reported trends are mostly qualitative in the supplied text, with several results presented in figures and no uncertainty estimates stated. The authors note that trajectory-coherence relationships appear less linear in some settings and plan future tests across domains, architectures, and algorithms.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible result rows identified.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label held-out generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the role of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under limited or broader tuning.
Large versus small batches under matched epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects, small-data regimes, underfitting, and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, including comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removal of highly memorized examples versus equal-sized random removal.

record.verdict_notes: The exclusion from V7 rests on the different sharpness measure and outcome, not merely the use of meta-learning or different datasets. States are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions; the adjacent findings remain recorded under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures, and the specified CIFAR-10/SVHN setting.
Removing memorized examples and the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: MAML and First-Order MAML
rows.operation_detail: Measured spectral norm of the Hessian at adapted meta-test solutions as training progressed.

conditions.value: 5-way and 20-way Omniglot; 5-way MiniImagenet; 1-shot and 5-shot as applicable

rows.measure: Average spectral norm of support-loss Hessian at adapted solutions
rows.value: Solutions become flatter on average as meta-training progresses.
rows.note: A fixed set of 60 randomly sampled meta-test tasks was used after each epoch; five independent runs are described in the experimental setup.
rows.check: Unscaled support-loss Hessian curvature does not measure V7. The trajectory description also needs qualification: solutions initially become sharper, reach a peak, then become flatter.

rows.subject: First-Order MAML, MiniImagenet 5-way 1-shot
rows.operation_detail: Compared curvature of adapted solutions with meta-test target accuracy during extended training.
rows.measure: Target accuracy and spectral norm of support-loss Hessian
rows.value: As generalization starts to degrade, the solutions keep getting flatter.
rows.note: The text identifies this as the model that appeared most likely to overfit.
rows.check: The reported deterioration in target accuracy despite decreasing Hessian curvature is an adjacent finding, not a reversal of V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–gap relationship.

rows.subject: Finetuning baseline
rows.stage_stated: pretrained on meta-training classes; adapted to meta-test tasks
rows.operation_detail: Measured curvature of adapted solutions and compared its training progression with the meta-learning algorithms.
rows.measure: Spectral norm of Hessian at adapted solutions
rows.value: The opposite trend occurs: solutions become sharper as training progresses.
rows.note: Authors suggest flatness may be more linked to support loss for this baseline, which they say is not an indicator of generalization.
rows.check: Increasing unscaled Hessian curvature during finetuning does not establish an opposite effect for any listed version.

rows.subject: MAML and First-Order MAML
rows.operation_detail: Measured average inner product between meta-test trajectory direction vectors and compared it with target accuracy.

conditions.value: Few-shot classification settings; full settings referenced in Figures 5 and 10

rows.measure: Average inner product between trajectory direction vectors; meta-test target accuracy
rows.value: Higher average inner product between trajectory directions is linked to higher average target accuracy; the paper reports the same observations in other settings.
rows.locator: Sections 5.2 and Appendix B.2, Figures 5 and 10
rows.note: The text notes that for some other settings the relationship appears less linear. For trajectory coherence, 500 tasks were sampled after each meta-training epoch.
rows.check: Trajectory-direction coherence measures none of the listed versions. Conditions should specify that First-Order MAML was omitted from the Omniglot trajectory-coherence analyses.

rows.subject: Finetuning baseline
rows.stage_stated: pretrained on meta-training classes; adapted to meta-test tasks
rows.operation_detail: Measured average inner product between meta-test trajectory direction vectors alongside target accuracy.
rows.measure: Average inner product between trajectory direction vectors
rows.value: The measure remains much closer to zero, with trajectory directions roughly orthogonal; target accuracies are much lower than for the meta-learning methods.
rows.note: The paper gives no exact numeric values in the text.
rows.check: Low trajectory coherence and lower target accuracy are adjacent findings; 'partial' has no applicable claim version here.

rows.subject: MAML and First-Order MAML
rows.operation_detail: Measured average inner product between meta-test gradient vectors at the meta-train solution against target accuracy.

conditions.value: Few-shot classification settings; full settings referenced in Figures 7 and 11

rows.measure: Average inner product between meta-test gradients; meta-test target accuracy
rows.value: Higher average inner product is linked to better generalization; authors say the metric consistently correlates with generalization across settings.
rows.note: Figure 7 shows individual model runs rather than averages over runs.
rows.check: Gradient coherence is not a listed measure. Specify that these experiments used one adaptation step during both meta-training and meta-testing.

rows.subject: Finetuning baseline
rows.stage_stated: pretrained on meta-training classes; adapted to meta-test tasks
rows.operation_detail: Measured coherence between meta-test gradient vectors.
rows.measure: Average inner product between meta-test gradients
rows.value: The paper reports very low coherence.
rows.note: No exact numeric value is given in the text.
rows.check: Low gradient coherence does not measure an incomplete effect under any listed version.

rows.subject: MAML with proposed regularizer
rows.operation_detail: Added a regularization term based on coherence of adaptation trajectories, with coefficient γ = 0.5.

conditions.value: 600 test tasks; average over five trials

rows.note: Authors report approximately 23% relative reduction in meta-test target error.
rows.check: The accuracy values are correctly reported, but this is the study's proposed regularizer compared with unregularized MAML. It belongs under fits_no_version, rather than as evidence for a listed version.

rows.subject: MAML
rows.operation_detail: Measured average norm of meta-test adaptation trajectories over training.
rows.measure: Average L2 norm of meta-test adaptation trajectories
rows.value: The norm grows as meta-training progresses for MAML, unlike the Finetune baseline; authors say it does not reflect generalization.
rows.note: The paper reports a trend but does not give exact numeric values in the text.
rows.check: Adaptation trajectory norm is distinct from all listed measures; the authors' statement that it does not reflect generalization cannot establish absence of a listed effect.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
